title: Valency and Oxidation States Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Water is H2O, natural gas is mostly CH4 and common salt is NaCl. Why does oxygen hold two hydrogens, carbon four, and sodium just one chlorine? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 3, Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties) we find the counting rule behind every formula.

You will see sodium hand its one valence electron to chlorine, then watch the molecule bench build CH4, NH3, H2O and HF as hydrogens snap onto carbon, nitrogen, oxygen and fluorine (valency 4, 3, 2, 1) while the valence table fills in. We predict SiBr4 from group numbers, then build oxidation state step by step on OF2 and Na2O, where oxygen is +2 in one and -2 in the other because of electronegativity. A worked example gives Al2S3 and checks it with oxidation states, then we meet variable valency and the ion [AlCl(H2O)5]2+, where covalency is 6 but the oxidation state is +3. Then the exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 35 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
